name: CGameSprite::RunAwayFrom
needs: The exe fetches the attacking weapon as in_ECX[*(byte *)(in_ECX + 0x12e9) + 0x12b6] (bundle i048/0x744C00.md, CGameSprite::RunAwayFrom): m_equipment.m_items (0x12b6*4 = 0x4AD8) indexed by the BYTE at CGameSprite+0x12E9, with the ITEM_ABILITY read from 0x4BA6 = m_equipment.m_selectedWeaponAbility. Our tree declares no member at 0x12E9: m_derivedStats (@0x920, size 0xE58... spans to 0x1778) models that byte as m_derivedStats.m_spells + 0x41D, i.e. inside m_spellsByClass[7] CGameSpriteGroupedSpellList spellbook data, so the exe's weapon-slot byte cannot be named without a CGameSprite/CDerivedStats layout change, which is outside the declaration-only header edits this batch allows. The fork body instead uses m_equipment.m_items[m_equipment.m_selectedWeapon] (m_selectedWeapon = m_equipment+0xCC = byte 0x4BA4), and the fork's own tree models m_equipment @0x4AD8 identically (fork src/CGameSprite.h line 882), so its body reads a different byte than the exe does - a fork-vs-exe divergence, not a build assumption. Everything else in the body is exe-faithful and ready to land once a member for byte 0x12E9 exists: the ACTION_NORMAL/ACTION_INTERRUPTABLE return ternary equals the exe's (m_curAction.m_actionID != 0xB8) under our CGameAibBase statics (no RUNAWAYFROMNOINTERRUPT constant exists in our tree either, needs a 0xB8 literal + comment), the sanctuary test m_spellStates[SPLSTATE_SANCTUARY] equals the exe's bit 0x100000 at +0xA0C, the 120/240/120 far-path phases with GRID_SQUARE_SIZE offsets and rand()%2 axis flip, the GetNearest range (SHORT)((space + range) * 0x10) via dead-CONCAT truncation, the nAreaX/nAreaY clamps (0x54C/0x550), the GetShare retry loop against SHARED/DENIED with THREAD_ASYNCH/INFINITE, and the DropPath/SetSequence messages on the field_5614 reset
